claim: Arena bounds: CEILNG is $0020 — the highest position in the game. HEX. The ceiling test compares only the HIGH byte of the 16-bit position, so it is a whole-pixel threshold.

source.verbatim: CEILNG	EQU	$0020		CEILING (HIGHEST POSITION) OF GAME)

claim: Arena bounds: FLOOR is $00DF — the lowest position. Lava death is a further 7 pixels below this (FLOOR+7 = 230).

source.verbatim: FLOOR	EQU	$00DF		THE FLOOR (LOWEST POSITION OF GAME)

claim: Arena bounds: ELEFT is -10, the extreme left of the wrap-around screen. DECIMAL and NEGATIVE — a reader that treats a leading minus as a symbol cannot resolve it at all.

source.verbatim: ELEFT	EQU	-10		EXTREME LEFT SIDE OF WRAP AROUND SCREEN

claim: Arena bounds: ERIGHT is 292, the extreme right of the wrap-around screen. DECIMAL. ERIGHT-ELEFT+1 = 303 is the wrap correction step.

source.verbatim: ERIGHT	EQU	292		EXTREME RIGHT SIDE OF WRAP AROUND SCREEN

claim: Arena bounds: MAXVX is 8, the maximum X velocity. This is why the ROM's single-correction wrap and a modulus agree for everything the game can actually produce — and why writing the modulus would ship green.
X wrap: WRAPX compares the new X against ERIGHT and, per the BLE on the next line, subtracts the span ONCE if it is past. There is no loop and no modulus.

X wrap: the single right-side correction is a subtract of ERIGHT-ELEFT+1 = 303, applied at most once. On a large delta the result can legally remain outside the range (600 -> 297), which a modulus would never produce.
X wrap: the left-side comparison against ELEFT uses BGE on the following line, so ELEFT itself is a legal position — the bounds do not wrap.
X wrap: the single left-side correction adds the same 303 span, again at most once.
Ceiling: ADDGRX compares the whole-pixel Y against CEILNG. Only the HIGH byte is tested, so a fraction cannot tip an entity over the boundary.
Ceiling: BHI skips the whole ceiling handler when the position is strictly above the ceiling — so contact is at-or-past, not past.

source.verbatim: BHI	ADGCEI		 BR=HAVE NOT HIT CEILING

claim: Ceiling: BPL skips the velocity negation when the entity is ALREADY moving down. An entity descending through the ceiling band keeps its velocity; flipping it would fling it back up and trap it there.

source.verbatim: BPL	ADGDWN		 BR=ALREADY GOING DOWN, DON'T GO UP

claim: Ceiling: COMA/NEGB/SBCA #-1 is exact 16-bit two's-complement negation of the velocity — elastic with no damping.

Ceiling: ADGDWN loads CEILNG*256 UNCONDITIONALLY, so the position is CLAMPED to exactly CEILING<<8 with the fraction zeroed — however far past the ceiling the step went. A mirroring implementation drifts from the ROM within one frame.
Lava death: ADGCEI compares the whole-pixel Y against FLOOR+7 = 230.

source.verbatim: ADGCEI	CMPA	#FLOOR+7	BELOW SEA LEVEL (ON THE FLOOR)?

claim: Lava death: BHS is unsigned higher-or-same, so the threshold is at-or-below on whole pixels — one pixel short with a full fraction still lives.

source.verbatim: BHS	ADGFLR		 BR=YES, TOO BAD, YOU ARE DEAD

claim: Landing: CKGND ANDs the LNDXTB column mask with the LNDYTB scanline mask; a non-zero result means the entity is starting to land on a cliff, and the background-collision path is then skipped entirely.

source.verbatim: LDA	LNDXTB,X	STARTING TO LAND ON A CLIFF?

claim: Background collision: BCKXTB/BCKYTB is a SEPARATE box broad-phase, reached only when the landing masks produce nothing. Its bit assignment differs from the landing table's.

source.verbatim: LDA	BCKXTB,X	BACKGROUND MAP IN X DIRECTION

claim: Landing dispatch: the first split is CMPA #$08 — below goes to the LND13 group, equal is LNDB3, above is the LND47 group.
Landing dispatch: the second split is CMPA #$20, with values below it landing on CLIF4.

Landing dispatch: CLIF5 is selected by a BIT test, not equality — LNDYTB never holds a bare $20 because CLIF5's band is $A0 (bit 7 | bit 5). A dispatch written as bit-per-platform equality misses CLIF5 entirely and drops entities through the bottom island.
Landing dispatch: the fall-through when bit 5 is absent is LNDB7, the lava troll's grip — the SEVENTH outcome. Bit 7 WITHOUT bit 5 means the troll, not a platform.
Landing dispatch: within the low group, BHI sends masks 3..7 to LNDB2 while 1 falls through to LNDB0 and 2 branches to LNDB1.
Landing snap: LNDB0 (CLIF1L & CLIF1R) assigns whole-pixel Y $0045-1 = 68 — one pixel above its LNDYTB band top of 69, i.e. the entity rests ON the surface.

source.verbatim: LDB	#$0045-1	ON TOP OF CLIFF PIXEL HEIGHT

claim: Landing snap: LNDB1 (CLIF2) assigns $0051-1 = 80, one pixel above band top 81.

source.verbatim: LDB	#$0051-1	ON TOP OF CLIFF PIXEL HEIGHT

claim: Landing snap: LNDB2 assigns $0081-1 = 128, one pixel above band top 129 — which is CLIF3U's band. The author comment on the label line reads CLIF3R, but CLIF3R sits at 138 and is served by LNDB3. A transcription following comments instead of constants maps the wrong cliff to this bit.

source.verbatim: LDB	#$0081-1	ON TOP OF CLIFF PIXEL HEIGHT

claim: Landing snap: LNDB3 (CLIF3L & CLIF3R) assigns $008A-1 = 137, one pixel above band top 138.

source.verbatim: LDB	#$008A-1	ON TOP OF CLIFF PIXEL HEIGHT

claim: Landing snap: LNDB4 (CLIF4) assigns $00A3-1 = 162, one pixel above band top 163.

source.verbatim: LDB	#$00A3-1	ON TOP OF CLIFF PIXEL HEIGHT

claim: Landing snap: LNDB5 (CLIF5) assigns $00D3-1 = 210, one pixel above band top 211.

source.verbatim: LDB	#$00D3-1	ON TOP OF CLIFF PIXEL HEIGHT

claim: Landing is a SNAP: the whole-pixel Y is stored directly into the position and, on the following line, CLRA zeroes the fraction — nothing about the entry position or velocity survives, which is what makes landing idempotent.

Landing: LNDB7 is the lava trolls' handler, the seventh dispatch destination. Its behaviour is gated on TTROLL and belongs to a later story; the dispatch slot must exist now or the bitmask decision tree is wrong.
Bridge: TBRIDGE is seeded with 3 — the wave number at which the bridge is destroyed. DECIMAL.

source.verbatim: STA	TBRIDGE		WAVE NBR TO DESTROY BRIDGE

claim: Troll: TTROLL is seeded with 1 — the number of waves after the bridge is destroyed before the lava troll comes out into the open. DECIMAL.

source.verbatim: STA	TTROLL		 COMES OUT IN THE OPEN

claim: Lava: SAFRAM starts at $EA, the wave-1 lava surface level. HEX. Rising lava means DEcreasing Y.

source.verbatim: LDA	#$EA		START LEVEL OF LAVA FOR BUBBLING LAVA ROUTINE

claim: Lava rise: the per-wave step compares SAFRAM against $E0 and, per the BLS on the next line, stops there. The lava is a five-unit step with a hard floor, not an unbounded subtract.
Lava rise: each wave subtracts $5, producing exactly three distinct levels ($EA, $E5, $E0) before the guard holds it forever.
Bridge: TBRIDGE is decremented once per wave and, per the BEQ above, stops at zero — so the bridge burns on wave 3 and stays gone.
Background collision: BCKCOL is the cliff-side pixel path, entered from CKGND after the box broad-phase hits. This trace closes open-questions §4.
Background collision: BCKB0 dereferences CLIF1L's record indirectly to reach its collision-span pointer — the very tables jt1-3 transcribed — then walks them from a loaded origin.
Background collision: bit 0 walks CLIF1L from X origin -32. NEGATIVE DECIMAL: the left cliff starts off-screen to the left.
Background collision: bit 0 walks CLIF1L from Y origin 69, which is exactly CLIF1L's own record destination scanline — the same number stated in two unrelated places.

Background collision: bit 4 is CLIF3L here. In the LANDING table bit 4 is CLIF4 — the two mechanisms use DIFFERENT bit assignments (eight bits with left/right separate vs six with the pairs merged), so sharing one table between them collides against the wrong geometry.
Background collision: BCKB3 (bit 3 = CLIF3U) dereferences CLIF3R's collision pointer — not CLIF3U's.

Background collision: BCKB5 (bit 5 = CLIF3R) is BYTE-IDENTICAL to BCKB3 — the same CLIF3R pointer with CLIF3U's origin (202,129), even though CLIF3R sits at (254,138). Whether that is a shipped bug or deliberate reuse is not settled; the transcription PRESERVES it, because tidying it would silently change collision behaviour.
Background collision: bit 7 is CLIF5, walked from origin (54,211) — the bottom island, matching its record destination and NEWCL5's hard-coded start position.

Landing dispatch: the LNDB2 label line carries the author comment 'CLIF3R' — the comment that is WRONG. Its constant on the next line resolves to CLIF3U's band. Recorded so the hazard is anchored at the line a reader actually sees.
Landing dispatch: LNDB3's label line names both CLIF3L and CLIF3R, which is where CLIF3R is really served — one pixel above scanline 138, not LNDB2's 129.
Landing dispatch: LNDB4's label line names CLIF4. In the LANDING table bit 4 is CLIF4; in the BACKGROUND table the same bit is CLIF3L — the two mechanisms' bit assignments differ.
